result.note: Tests the August 2026 approval of DRDO missile technology transfer to private firms, the BDL baseline and the Pinaka export to Armenia.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the decision on DRDO missile technology announced in August 2026:
items: The Defence Minister approved transfers of DRDO technology for every conventional missile to qualified Indian companies.
The announcement named the specific missile systems and manufacturers that would receive the technology.
DRDO had transferred Astra Mk-I and its associated systems to Bharat Dynamics Limited in 2022.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the announcement names no systems, manufacturers, timetable or selection process, and firms must first pass certification. Until now, missile production after development has typically gone through state-owned Bharat Dynamics Limited.
questions.source: On Tuesday, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh approved transfers of Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) technology for every conventional missile to qualified Indian companies.

questions.prompt: Guided Pinaka rockets produced by the Indian private firm Solar Defence, cited in August 2026 as an example of private participation in missile production, were made for export to which country?
questions.explain: Solar Defence produced guided Pinaka rockets for export to Armenia, showing private participation was already underway. In June 2026 the Defence Minister had warned that production capacity now matters as much as research.
questions.source: Solar Defence produced guided Pinaka rockets for export to Armenia
